proves.claim: A claim whose seat heartbeats but made no non-renewal move or commit for 31 minutes is captured as an idle release with a handoff, and none at 29 minutes.

health.io-stale-state-capture.idle-30-re.why: Without it the idle release could keep waiting 40 minutes after the release table and the store re-check accept 30.

proves.claim: CLAIM_IDLE_RELEASE_MS equals 30 minutes.

health.logic-stale-state-query.idle-rele.why: Without it the idle claim release would stay at 40 minutes while the release table and store re-check accept 30.

proves.claim: A seat shout to the coordinator unanswered past health.stuck is one Stuck finding naming the shout, sender, item and age.

health.io-main-shouts.unanswered-stuck.why: Without it a builder's blocker shout can sit unanswered with nothing escalating it.

proves.claim: An answered shout, a young one and a coordinator shout give no unanswered-shout finding.

health.io-main-shouts.answered-or-young-.why: Without it the finding could fire on shouts that need no escalation.

proves.claim: healthLines prints the unanswered-shout finding the health report holds.

health.io-main-shouts.health-lines.why: Without it the finding could exist in the report and never reach the pullboard health output.

proves.claim: The board health line names the command, seat and held time of a live-board hold over 200 ms from the last hour.

health.holds.live-board-named.why: A slow live-board hold was not named on the health line.

proves.claim: Hold rows from other board files are not named.

health.holds.other-boards-ignored.why: Hold rows from other board files were reported as this board's.

proves.claim: With health.derivedState on, the sweep writes rows keyed by main commit and kind to a derived file beside the board, never the board database.

health.derived.sweep-writes-file.why: The sweep wrote derived rows into the board database.

proves.claim: The holds rows equal the holds the board reports for the same main commit.

health.derived.holds-match-board.why: Derived holds rows differed from the board's own holds.

proves.claim: With health.derivedState off the sweep writes no file.

health.derived.off-writes-nothing.why: With the setting off the sweep still wrote a file.

proves.claim: A refused batch shouts its item and code, then escalates after fifteen unanswered minutes.

health.landing.refused-shouts-escalates.why: A refused batch went unannounced or never escalated.

proves.claim: Only an explicit coordinator acknowledgement answers a landing failure.

health.landing.ack-coordinator-only.why: Anyone's reply silenced a landing failure.

proves.claim: A later landing retires the failed batch instead of raising a stale exception.

health.landing.later-landing-retires.why: A stale failed batch raised an exception after a later landing.

proves.claim: A refused batch whose items all landed by another path raises no finding, one still open does.

health.landing.landed-elsewhere-quiet.why: A batch whose items landed another way still raised a finding.

proves.claim: With moves.live.reclaim on, a pass over a quiet seat releases exactly the item and events the table names, the board the setting off leaves.

health.reclaim-live.table-releases.why: The live reclaim released a different item or events than the table named.

proves.claim: With moves.live.reclaim on, a row the table refuses is refused with the table's code and changes nothing.

health.reclaim-live.refusal-kept.why: A row the table refuses was changed anyway.

proves.claim: With moves.live.reclaim unset, the writer's own decision stands and the table runs only as the shadow compare.

health.reclaim-live.unset-shadow-only.why: With the setting unset the table overrode the writer's decision.

proves.claim: Strict uses current material authors, excluding earlier holders and removed companions from fresh review rules.

health.cover.strict-current-authors.why: Strict review excluded earlier holders or kept removed companions.

proves.claim: A current companion family stays excluded when a third joined family can independently review.

health.cover.companion-family-excluded.why: A current companion family could review the item.

proves.claim: Mixed-family composition remains independently reviewable while every current author and parent stays excluded.
Owner uses matching native submit size against active patch hunk lines; a tie retains last builder.

health.cover.owner-by-size.why: The owner ignored native submit size against patch hunk lines.

proves.claim: Old ordered review semantics still exclude historical contributors and refuse mixed-family reachability.

health.cover.old-ordered-semantics.why: Old ordered review semantics let historical contributors review.

proves.claim: Current strict local session checks ignore superseded ledger claims but still refuse current authors.

health.cover.superseded-claims.why: Superseded ledger claims blocked or admitted a session wrongly.

proves.claim: New native activation fences downgraded review while preserving genuine historical receipt bytes.

health.cover.native-activation-fence.why: Native activation changed genuine historical receipt bytes.

proves.claim: Real submit preflight uses candidate size for companion-owned reachability and rolls every observation back.
The scheduled sentinel sweep sends one durable nudge after 30 idle minutes and observes the 10-minute release plan.

health.sweep.nudge-after-idle.why: The sentinel sweep nudged more than once or at the wrong idle time.

proves.claim: The scheduled sentinel path runs stale-claim release before the watchdog nudge pass.

health.sweep.release-before-nudge.why: The watchdog nudged a claim that stale release should have freed.

proves.claim: A claim already marked stalled still reaches the watchdog when stale-state has no new action.

health.sweep.stalled-reaches-watchdog.why: A stalled claim with no new action never reached the watchdog.

proves.claim: A quiet seat whose own test run has waited 5 minutes for a runner keeps its claim.

health.capture.waiting-test-run-keeps.why: A seat waiting on a runner lost its claim.

proves.claim: A quiet seat whose runner check has run for 5 minutes under a live lease keeps its claim.

health.capture.runner-check-keeps.why: A seat with a running runner check lost its claim.

proves.claim: A quiet seat whose gate check is running on a runner keeps its claim.

health.capture.gate-check-keeps.why: A seat whose gate check was running lost its claim.

proves.claim: A quiet seat with no job in flight is still reclaimed at two minutes.

health.capture.no-job-reclaimed.why: A quiet seat with no job stayed claimed.

proves.claim: Finished, lapsed, long-queued or other-seat jobs do not keep a quiet claim.

health.capture.dead-jobs-dont-keep.why: Finished or foreign jobs kept a quiet claim.

proves.claim: A test run queued from an item folder records that item on its job, so the quiet holder keeps its claim.

health.capture.item-folder-run-keeps.why: A run queued from an item folder did not keep its holder's claim.

proves.claim: A lapsed-claim pass that keeps every lapsed claim and leaves the scan cursor where it is captures nothing, so no maintenance write opens.

health.capture.vetoed-lapse-no-write.why: Every CLI write opened a maintenance write that changed nothing.

proves.claim: A lapsed-claim pass still captures when the scan cursor would move or a claim row needs a decision.

health.capture.cursor-move-still-capture.why: A pass that had a cursor to move or a claim to decide captured nothing.

proves.claim: A lapsed-claim pass over several claims reads the waiting dependents once, not once per claim row.

health.capture.waiters-read-once.why: Every board write spent about 16 s running the dependents query once per claim row.

proves.claim: The once-per-pass waited set names exactly the ids the per-id dependents query finds.

health.capture.waiters-same-answer.why: The once-per-pass read could miss or invent a waiting dependent.

proves.claim: Three red gates with unaccounted failures within an hour raise one Stuck shout naming the gates and the first unparsed line.

health.detector.three-reds-stuck.why: Three unaccounted red gates raised no Stuck shout.

proves.claim: Red gates whose failures are fully accounted raise no shout.

health.detector.accounted-quiet.why: Fully accounted reds raised a shout.

proves.claim: One unaccounted red among a handful of accounted reds stays quiet below 20 percent.

health.detector.under-20-percent-quiet.why: One unaccounted red among many accounted raised a shout.

proves.claim: With moves.shadow on, a pass that releases a quiet seat records one reclaim compare that agrees with the release it wrote.

health.reclaim-shadow.records-compare.why: A release recorded no reclaim compare or one that disagreed.

proves.claim: With moves.shadow off, a pass runs no reclaim table and records nothing.

health.reclaim-shadow.off-records-nothin.why: With shadow off a pass still ran the reclaim table.

proves.claim: With claim.keepWhileRunning on, a claim past the idle release with a live test-run, test or gate job on its item is not returned.

health.running-run.keep-while-running.why: A claim with a live run on its item was returned.

proves.claim: With claim.keepWhileRunning at its default (off) the same claim is returned as today, and a claim with no job in flight is still returned with it on.

health.running-run.default-off.why: The default changed what is returned.

proves.claim: Claim health carries building, stalled, waiting and unknown-idle claims from the board read.

health.activity.claim-health-states.why: Claim health lost building, stalled, waiting or unknown-idle claims.

proves.claim: The projection reads a snapshot row into state, idle minutes, waiting ids and handoff pin.

health.activity.snapshot-projection.why: The projection misread a snapshot row.

proves.claim: Most claimed seats quiet together is a machine stall, a single quiet seat is not.

health.stall.machine-vs-single.why: A single quiet seat counted as a machine stall.

proves.claim: The real capture releases nothing when every claimed seat goes quiet together, and says so once.

health.stall.capture-releases-nothing.why: A machine stall released every claimed seat.

proves.claim: A single seat that misses alone is still released.

health.stall.lone-seat-released.why: A single missing seat was never released.

proves.claim: A sentinel tick that runs late is a machine stall even when one seat alone is quiet.

health.stall.late-tick-is-stall.why: A late sentinel tick released seats.

proves.claim: The real sweep releases a lone silent seat on time and holds it, with one machine-stall shout, when its own tick ran late.

health.stall.sweep-lone-seat-on-time.why: The sweep held a lone silent seat or shouted twice.

proves.claim: every health-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

health.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: Every health test file that reads repo files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

health.inputs.every-health-test-file-tha.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: With tests.requireDeclaredInputs on, no health test reads fixtures, data or docs without a header.

health.inputs.with-tests-requiredeclared.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: No import specifier in packages/health/src resolves to the landing barrel file.

health.landing-door.no-barrel-import.why: A barrel import pulled the whole landing cell into the status closure.

proves.claim: localReleaseRank from the light door is the barrel's function.

health.landing-door.same-function.why: The light door could drift from the barrel's function.

proves.claim: The sweep writes seat-family rows equal to the families the board records for the same main commit.

health.derived-gates.seat-family-matches.why: Derived seat-family rows differed from the families the board recorded.

proves.claim: The gate-at-head rows equal what gateAtHead computes for each queued item.

health.derived-gates.gate-at-head-matche.why: Derived gate-at-head rows differed from what gateAtHead computed.

proves.claim: One sweep writes all five kinds in one transaction, and a failure part-way writes none.

health.derived-gates.five-kinds-one-tran.why: A sweep could leave a commit with some kinds written and others missing.

proves.claim: With health.derivedState off the one sweep writes no file.

health.derived-gates.off-writes-nothing.why: The one sweep wrote a derived file with the setting off.

proves.claim: A relay credential within 3 days of expiry yields an expiring finding and an expired one an expired finding, each with one next command and no bearer value.

health.credential.expiring-and-expired.why: An expiring credential went unnamed, or its finding leaked the bearer value.

proves.claim: A credential 4 days from expiry yields no finding, nor does a link without an expiry.

health.credential.far-or-absent.why: Far-off or absent expiries raised findings nobody needed.

proves.claim: The verdict freshness rows equal what next computes for the same main commit.

health.derived-verdicts.freshness-matche.why: Derived freshness rows differed from what next computed.

proves.claim: The accept-order rows equal the board accept order for that commit.

health.derived-verdicts.accept-order-mat.why: Derived accept-order rows differed from the board's order.

proves.claim: A new main commit gets its own rows and leaves the old commit rows unread.

health.derived-verdicts.new-commit-own-r.why: A new commit overwrote or reused the old commit's rows.

proves.claim: With health.derivedState off the verdict sweep writes no file.

health.derived-verdicts.off-writes-no-fi.why: With the setting off the verdict sweep still wrote a file.

proves.claim: After the sweep at a main commit, readDerivedState returns the five kinds equal to the rows the sweep wrote.

health.derived-read.matches-sweep.why: The reader returned kinds that differed from the swept rows.

proves.claim: readDerivedState returns null for a never-swept commit, a moved-on commit, the setting off and an in-memory board, but not for a swept commit with only empty kinds.

health.derived-read.null-unless-current.why: A reader trusted a table that was not current for the main commit.

proves.claim: packages/health/light.js exports readDerivedState as the health index function, and its static import closure reaches no file outside packages/health and imports only node built-ins.

health.io-derived.light-door-reads-deriv.why: Without it the health door could pull in other cells or drift from the health index's function.

proves.claim: No import specifier in packages/health/src/io/main.js resolves to the stats barrel file.

health.io-main-door.no-barrel-import.why: A barrel import pulled the whole stats cell into the status closure.

proves.claim: readWorkFreeReleases from the stats light door is the barrel function.

health.io-main-door.same-function.why: The stats light door could drift from the barrel function.

proves.claim: sweepDerivedAtMain sweeps the derived table when it is not current at the main commit, returning the counts, and sweeps nothing once it is current.

health.derived-read.sweeps-only-when-not.why: Without it a main move could rewrite the table on every pass or never refresh it.

proves.claim: A claim whose seat shows no heartbeat, event or item-folder commit for 60 minutes gets one more consecutive-sweep count per sweep in board_meta, restarting on a new claim episode and on any sign of life, and the count survives a fresh board handle.

health.io-claim-sweep.counts-silent-swee.why: Without it the stall release has no durable proof that a seat stayed silent across sweeps.

proves.claim: A seat heartbeat or an item-folder commit inside the hour clears the silence count, and a claim that ended is no longer counted.

health.io-claim-sweep.sign-of-life-ends-.why: Without it a seat that is working could be counted silent and released.

proves.claim: sweepClaims records the silence count once per sweep on a real board.

health.io-claim-sweep.records-silence.why: Without it the counter could exist and never run on the production sentinel sweep.

proves.claim: A builder holding a live claim on its own rejected item gives no RANK_INVERSION finding while open work ranks ahead.

health.io-main-rank-inversion.own-rework.why: Without it the sentinel told a builder to release rejected work for new work, which loses its item folder.

proves.claim: A builder claiming a never-rejected item while open work ranks ahead still gives one RANK_INVERSION finding naming both.

health.io-main-rank-inversion.fresh-clai.why: Without it the own-rework exemption could silence every rank inversion.

proves.claim: A scratch volume under the tool-tree floor is one Stuck finding naming free MB, the floor, the folder and the lost main comparison.

health.io-main-disk.tool-tree-low.why: Without it review packets silently lose their main comparison and nothing tells the coordinator.

proves.claim: A null room reading gives no tool-tree finding.

health.io-main-disk.room-ok.why: Without it the finding could fire with plenty of room.

proves.claim: healthLines prints the tool-tree disk finding the health report holds.

health.io-main-disk.health-lines.why: Without it the finding could exist in the report and never reach the pullboard health output.

proves.claim: A submitted item whose review reservation lapsed is not read as held, so it gets NO_REVIEWER_SUPPLY.

health.io-supply.expired-reservation-not.why: Without it a lapsed reservation hides the shortage until someone releases it.

proves.claim: healthReport lists NO_REVIEWER_SUPPLY for a lapsed reservation on a fixture board and not while it is held.

health.io-supply.real-path.why: Without it supply.js could pass its unit case while main.js still passes no time-gated reader.

proves.claim: With health.adviceThroughNext on, a claim reserved to its holder yields no RANK_INVERSION finding and an unreserved claim still yields one.

health.io-main.reserved-claim-no-release.why: Keeps a reserved claim from drawing release advice only when the advice setting is on.

proves.claim: With the setting off or unset, the reserved claim yields the RANK_INVERSION finding as before.

health.io-main.reserved-claim-setting-of.why: Keeps a reserved claim from drawing release advice only when the advice setting is on.

proves.claim: With health.adviceThroughNext on, a claim whose item has a hold reason yields no RANK_INVERSION finding and the same board without a hold reason still yields one.

health.io-main.held-claim-no-release-adv.why: Keeps a coordinator-held claim from drawing release advice that the coordinator placed on purpose.

proves.claim: With the setting off or unset, the held claim yields the RANK_INVERSION finding as before.

health.io-main.held-claim-setting-off.why: Keeps a held claim from drawing release advice only when the advice setting is on.

proves.claim: The clock table has the ten rows, each with an owner, a deadline or the lease or root it inherits, a default move and a one-deadline unknown limit, and clockRow maps every non-terminal fact set to exactly one row and throws for facts no row covers.

health.logic-clock-table.every-state-has.why: Without it an item state could have no owner or deadline, so nothing would ever move it and the board could jam.

proves.claim: clockDue is not due before the deadline, is due at one deadline on idle evidence, waits one more deadline on unknown evidence and is due at two deadlines whatever the evidence.

health.logic-clock-table.unknown-waits-o.why: Without it unknown activity evidence could hold an item forever instead of for one extra deadline.

proves.claim: One clock pass applies the registered move of each due item, logs one clock_move event by the board with rule, state, move, since, deadlineAt and evidence, reports unregistered moves as pending without applying them, and a second pass at the same now applies nothing.

health.io-clock-sweep.applies-due-moves.why: Without it a due state could sit past its deadline unseen, or a repeated pass could shout the same deadline twice.

proves.claim: clockSweep with dryRun true returns one versioned result with applied, pending and waiting lists and writes no event.

health.io-clock-sweep.dry-run-writes-not.why: Without it a dry run meant to preview the clock's moves could change the board.

proves.claim: clockHealth counts an open item that matches no clock row as without owner and deadline and names its id, and reports the overdue count, the oldest overdue minutes and per-rule counts with their next deadline and move.

health.io-clock-health.counts-missing-ow.why: Without it an item no clock row covers could sit unseen, so the invariant that every item has an owner and a deadline could not be measured.

proves.claim: Each clockSweep pass stores the health document in board meta key clock.health with the pass time and shouts the coordinator once per item that lacks an owner or deadline, never twice for the same item.

health.io-clock-health.stored-and-alarme.why: Without it status and the watch would have nothing stored to read, and the coordinator would not learn of an item the clock cannot move.

proves.claim: A coordinator hold with no deadline and no evidence goes to the re-bar queue one extra deadline after its first deadline: re-bar prefix keeps the original text, owner is the re-bar queue with a fresh deadline a day out, one clock_move, still held.

health.io-clock-moves-hold.coordinator-h.why: Coordinator holds never expired, so 96 items sat held for a median 41 hours.

proves.claim: A hold at 1439 min and a hold with a recorded deadline still in the future are left unchanged.

health.io-clock-moves-hold.before-limit-.why: Without it the move could re-bar a hold before its deadline or ignore a recorded deadline.

proves.claim: A re-scope release 121 min old with no later edit is held for the person: owner person, a deadline a day out, a reason quoting the release's seat, code, text and age, one clock_move; the clock never moves a person-owned hold.

health.io-clock-moves-rescope.to-person-.why: INELIGIBLE never expired, so re-scoped items stayed hidden forever; the person's list needs them and nothing automatic may decide them.

proves.claim: The same re-scope release at 119 min, or with a later edit event, is not moved.

health.io-clock-moves-rescope.cleared-or.why: Without it the move could hold an item before its deadline or after someone cleared it.

proves.claim: keepClaimWork writes keep/<id> at the item folder HEAD and, with uncommitted changes, a dirty handoffs ref, returns both names, and reports unsaved without throwing when the folder or HEAD is missing.

health.io-stale-state-capture.keep-write.why: Without it a released claim could lose its uncommitted work when the item folder is removed.

proves.claim: captureLapsedClaims puts keepClaimWork's result on the release rows it returns, next to the handoff.

health.io-stale-state-capture.keep-on-re.why: Without it the saved work would exist but no release row would name it.
